title: Hidden Gauge Freedom in Complex-Pole Hierarchical Equations of Motion
abstract: While complex-pole hierarchical equations of motion (HEOM) have dramatically expanded the reach of numerically exact quantum dynamics simulations of open quantum systems, they suffer from numerical instabilities rooted in the non-Hermitian structure of their Liouvillian. Yet, the origin of this structure remains obscure. Here, we report a previously unknown gauge freedom in complex-pole HEOM: a continuous family of analytically equivalent Liouvillians, all encoding the same bath correlation function, whose numerical properties vary dramatically. This gauge controls both the eigenspectrum and non-normality of the hierarchy generator, revealing spectral divergence and non-normal error amplification as two distinct instability mechanisms. By optimizing this gauge, we introduce GO--HEOM, which eliminates divergences in strongly coupled Brownian oscillator environments and extends numerically exact simulations of sub-Ohmic dynamics -- including through the delocalized-to-localized quantum phase transition -- to previously inaccessible coupling strengths. Because this gauge transformation is independent of the bath-correlation decomposition scheme, our GO--HEOM becomes a general, broadly compatible strategy for accessing numerically exact quantum dynamics of open quantum systems over arbitrary coupling and highly non-Markovian regimes.
summary: This paper reveals a previously unknown 'hidden gauge freedom' within the complex-pole HEOM formalism used for open quantum systems. By optimizing this gauge parameter, the authors introduce GO-HEOM, a method that significantly enhances numerical stability. This allows researchers to simulate strongly coupled or highly non-Markovian dynamics regimes that were previously inaccessible due to computational instabilities.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is the numerical instability inherent in complex-pole Hierarchical Equations of Motion (HEOM) when simulating open quantum systems.
main_result: The authors discovered a hidden gauge freedom within the HEOM formulation, allowing them to construct GO-HEOM which eliminates spectral divergences and extends simulations into previously inaccessible strongly coupled or sub-Ohmic regimes.
method: They analyze the structure of the Liouvillian generator by identifying a continuous gauge transformation parameter ($\phi$) that preserves physical dynamics while optimizing numerical stability metrics like non-normality.
model_or_system: The work focuses on open quantum systems, using the spin-boson model as a primary benchmark. The theory is developed around the complex-pole decomposition of the bath correlation function $C(t)$.
key_observables: Time evolution of observables like $\langle\sigma_z(t)angle$, spectral divergence indicators, and non-normal error amplification metrics ($\eta_H$).
important_parameters: Coupling strengths ($\alpha$), bath spectral density exponents ($s$ for sub-Ohmic), and the gauge-scaling parameter ($\phi_r$).
main_assumptions: The instability mechanisms (spectral divergence vs. non-normal amplification) are treated as distinct, controllable issues via the gauge transformation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the comparison of dynamics using conventional HEOM versus GO-HEOM across various coupling regimes, demonstrating stability improvements and convergence with respect to the optimization parameters.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the numerical instability problem in complex-pole HEOM. It then derives the existence of a gauge freedom ($\phi$) that parameterizes equivalent Liouvillians. Finally, it optimizes this gauge to create GO-HEOM and validates its superior performance across various non-Markovian spectral densities.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, general mathematical tool (the gauge optimization) to push the boundaries of numerically exact quantum dynamics simulations for open systems, which is crucial for modeling realistic quantum materials and environments.
